t:
Yes, I have heard of such a town. White 17 is a secret military town hidden somewhere deep in the astral. And, as far as I know, there is plenty there to hide. You see, in White 17 Imperial scientists were working on extremely dangerous projects. I don't know for certain, but rumour has it that Nomarkh Ebol, the lead researcher, maintained very close ties with Yasskul Setnakhte. And I have already told you about Yasskul Setnakhte and the incident at Lab Nine.

And recently contact with White 17 was lost. Completely. Not a letter, not a messenger, not a single word... I fear some disaster may have happened there, like the one that befell General Plague and his men. So if in your wanderings you come across a snowbound island guarded by Imperial soldiers, you had better turn back at once. But if you do risk landing there and get into trouble, look for Valentin Shtammin, an acquaintance of mine. I believe he is listed there as chief mechanic. Oh, my heart tells me something is wrong with that White 17…

Bosses: Distemper, Venomisk, Crunch, Nomarkh Ebol.

Climate: Tundra, closest to Coldberg.

Affiliation: Imperial allod, a secret laboratory.

Story:

t:
I happened to go there as part of a missionary and enlightenment mission. You see, White Mountain is home to a tribe of utterly savage goblins. The poor wretches don't even know who the Great Nezeb is! A thoroughly benighted people, and aggressive into the bargain! They wanted to sacrifice our missionaries to some scaly beast that the local goblins consider — just imagine — a god! Sacrilege, pure and simple!

When the missionaries and I left the island, a punitive detachment of the Committee arrived there to instil in the filthy heathens the fundamentals of the true faith, mutual respect and reverence for the Trinity Church.

What happened on the island I do not know, but I do know that the Committee men came back from it thoroughly battered and as angry as a thousand dragons, after which the island's coordinates and the records of the two expeditions the Empire had made to White Mountain were classified.

But from rumours and gossip I heard of some idol that the shaggy savage runts worship and which supposedly gave its servants the strength to overcome seasoned Imperial fighters.

If your path leads to White Mountain, remember: fanatics do not heed the voice of reason. Brute force is the only thing they understand well!

Bosses: Mosol, Potbelly, Kazhetan, I'do-ol.

Climate: Temperate, closest to Gipat.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by goblins.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

They wanted to sacrifice our missionaries to some scaly creature which the local goblins consider — just imagine — a god! Sacrilege, pure and simple!

When the missionaries and I left the island, a punitive detachment of the Committee arrived there to instil in the filthy pagans the fundamentals of the true faith, mutual respect and reverence for the Trinity Church. What happened on the island I do not know, but I do know that the Committee men came back from the island thoroughly battered and as furious as a thousand dragons, after which the coordinates of the island and the records of the two expeditions the Empire had made to the White Mountain were classified. Bosses: Mosol, Potbelly, Kazhetan, I'do-ol.

t:
In my travels I always steer clear of Wolf Isle. An ancient legend connected with this accursed place tells of a Kanian village that became a feasting hall for a werewolf.

They say that long, long ago a Kanian druid named Vseslav the Charming grew so close to the wolves living on the island that he learned to change into wolf form. He became the leader of the pack, and his neighbours its first victims. In time no one was left there but wolves and werewolves. Luckless travellers who risk landing on the island become a welcome treat for its inhabitants.

If you long to perform a heroic deed, Wolf Isle is a fitting place. But here is my advice: think a hundred times before you challenge the pack!

Bosses: Chernobog, the Bane of Wolf Isle, Vseslav the Charming.

Climate: Temperate, closest to Darkwater.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, formerly Kanian.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

In my wanderings I always give Wolf Isle a wide berth. An ancient legend tied to this deadly place tells of a Kanian village that became a feeding ground for a werewolf. They say that long, long ago a Kanian druid named Vseslav the Charming grew so close to the wolves living on the island that he learned to change into wolf shape. He became the leader of the pack, and his neighbours its first victims. In time nobody was left there but wolves and werewolves. Hapless travellers who dare to land on the island become a welcome treat for its inhabitants. If you long to perform a heroic deed, Wolf Isle is quite a fitting place. But here is my advice: think a hundred times before you challenge the pack!

Bosses: Chernobog, the Bane of Wolf Isle, Vseslav the Charming.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Addendum: Based on the Umoir Shard.

t:
Climate: Tropical, closest to Asee-Teph.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by the Waterfolk Tribe.

Story:

The allod was part of the Holy Land, like the Isle of the Dead; it broke off for unknown reasons. After landing and walking a little way, we come to a village of neutral Waterfolk. Rogoz (the chief of the neutral Waterfolk) speaks with us; he says that in the other settlements on this allod they still believe that the Whale-Fish saved the allod during the great splash, and they believed it too, until their prophet Seke the Sensible fell asleep at the altar in the center of the allod. He began to see visions and to enlighten us Waterfolk; he managed to tell… Our chief Bagor did not believe him and wants to sacrifice him. We agree to help him. We free Seke the Sensible. He says that he saw us in his visions, and also: "I dreamed a lot of things. I understood almost nothing. I dreamed of some dreadful creature with a big beard, chained to the sky. I dreamed of some monsters with tentacles on their faces... Oh, it's so complicated" (it is obvious to us that this is about Sarn). He also asks us to kill Bagor, who is preparing the place for the sacrifice. After our victory over Bagor, Seke the Sensible says that in another dream we defeat the Whale-Fish. And in yet another dream he becomes the leader on this boat-island. True, he refuses the power, but he still asks us to kill the Fish. After the victory Seke the Sensible says: "Now the lake turtles will gnaw the Whale-Fish's bones clean! It won't devour my people anymore!"

Bosses: Bagor, chief of the Waterfolk; Rybko the Whale-Fish.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Addendum: Over time it was reworked into the Shard of Power.

t:
Climate: Temperate, closest to Lightwood.

Affiliation: League allod, a Kanian colony.

Story:

We are met by serfs. They tell us that everything is fine on their island and that the allod is run by the lady Verona de Doucer. But in a whisper they ask us to go to the north of the allod and question the fugitives, for in truth they are oppressed here. At the astral shipyard we are met by Borodai Zalesky, a man of standing on the allod, who advises us to be sure to go to the lady. Verona tells us that she was invited here by Gordei Zalesky, but he died in her arms for unknown reasons, and his nephew asked her to stay and help run the allod. Gordei had invited other races to the allod — Gibberlings, orcs and so on — so that they would help the allod develop, but after his death they began to stir up unrest. We reach the fugitives' camp; there the Gibberlings tell the whole truth: the lady has set up a dictatorship, keeps everyone as slaves, they work themselves to the bone, and they are left only enough provisions to survive, but no more. The lady's troops had been spying on us; they attacked us, but we dealt with them. The Gibberling tells us the plan: he will raise the people against the remaining soldiers, and we are required to kill the lady, and the island will become free. As we approach the lady, we run into the voivode Zaruba Zalesky, and he has to be killed. A dialogue with Verona takes place, in which she says we are idiots and that she is the one holding the allod together, sends us to kill the chief conspirator, Otrad Zalesky, and goes off herself to calm the people.

After thinking over what had happened, the Gibberling shared his theory: the allod somehow held together even without the lady, so apparently Otrad was the one holding it, and he was most likely stupefied because of the golems the lady had brought with her. We stand at a crossroads: either we help return the allod to Otrad — switching off the golems, restoring his reason and killing Verona — or we kill Otrad and leave the island, for Verona no longer wants to see us on it.

Bosses: Zaruba Zalesky, Otrad Zalesky or Verona de Doucer.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Addendum: Over time the story was changed somewhat.

t: I've been to this island. Bliss: green forests, singing streams... A settlement stands there — bigger than a village, smaller than a town. Red walls, a church with a bell tower, prosperous and friendly people. In a word, it's pleasant to visit and you can trade at a profit. They say, though, that some bandits have recently started threatening them. Well, they're not poor folk — they have enough gold to hire mercenaries for help. Or maybe you'll help them, show some heroism?

I have been to that island. Bliss: green forests, singing streams... There stands a posad — bigger than a village, smaller than a town. Red walls, a church with a bell tower, people prosperous and friendly. In a word, it is pleasant to visit and profitable to trade there. They say, though, that some bandits have recently begun to threaten them. Well, they are not poor people — they have enough gold to hire mercenaries. Or perhaps you will help them and show some heroism?

Bosses: Forest Bear, Penny Pincher, Mira Hooves, Newsor Rotheart.

Climate: Temperate, closest to Lightwood.

Affiliation: League allod, inhabited by Kanians.

Story:

Astral island:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

I have been on that island. Bliss: green forests, singing streams... There stands a posad — bigger than a village, smaller than a town. Red walls, a church with a bell tower, prosperous and friendly people. In a word, it is pleasant to visit and profitable to trade there. True, they say some bandits have recently started threatening them. Well, they are not poor folk — they have enough gold to hire mercenaries. Or perhaps you will help them, show some heroism? We clear the allod, kill the bandits, and at the end the warlock too.

Story allod:

Catherina sent the Heroes to this island to obtain a real Firebird. The heroes set off. But an adventure awaited them as if they had truly stepped into a fairy tale. For first they clashed with dashing bandits who were robbing the villagers. They dealt with them and rescued the headman, who told them that the local druid, Nikodim Farouche, had the bird. And for his rescue the headman gave them a horse which could be traded for the bird. But on the way a werewolf attacked the heroes and devoured the horse; defeated, however, it promised to enter their service. Nikodim, of course, refused to simply hand over the bird and demanded another such horse, one that belonged to the local sorcerer — Mira Hooves. So the heroes went to Mira Hooves. For the horse he demanded that they perform three services for him. At first he asked them to do all sorts of nonsense, and then he gave them a hard task — the warlock Newsor Rotheart, he said, had abducted a maiden whom Mira Hooves wanted to take as his bride.

The heroes had to go and fight the warlock. Though he commanded the dead, he was nevertheless defeated and fled in disgrace. They returned to Mira Hooves with the rescued maiden, Milava Clairante. But he had already forgotten the bargain — so they had to calm him down too. Taking the horse, they went to Nikodim, but he too wanted Milava for himself. So he also had to be given a punch on the nose. And when they finally came to the pier with the bird, the two Gubarevsky brothers were waiting there, wanting to take the Firebird for themselves and bring it to Catherina themselves. They had to be dealt with as well.

Bosses:

Astral island: Forest Bear, Penny Pincher, Mira Hooves, Newsor Rotheart.

Story island: Newsor Rotheart, Nikodim Farouche, the Gubarevsky brothers.

Type: Medium island. Dungeon. Astral island. Umoir Archipelago. Story allod.

t:
From afar this island looks like a fairy tale from a distant childhood. Emerald greenery spreads out like a carpet, the peaceful singing of birds caresses the ear, and the friendly sun gently warms the earth. But be careful: this island hides many secrets, and it is not as simple as it seems at first glance.

Bosses: Scar, Kiddo, Crash, Nomarkh Sadaffee.

Climate: Tropical, closest to …

Affiliation: Imperial allod, the site of a laboratory.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

And why are you suddenly interested in Zone 51? You are not even supposed to know the name "Zone 51". It is classified information, I'll have you know! But I think that you, as a direct participant in the events at Laboratory 13, have the right to hear the truth about this secret military base of the Empire in the distant Astral. Listen carefully, and mind you don't let it slip! Zone 51 is a military laboratory in which, after the incident at Laboratory 13, experiments continued on the study of psychic influence on the mass consciousness. Nomarkh Sadaffee, the head of the project, decided to combine psionic influence with physical modification of the body. In his opinion, the imperfect human organism is not able to fully manipulate even its own consciousness, let alone influence others. And so he decided to combine the prosthetic technologies of the Arisen with psionic abilities. The combat mechanisms that resulted, controlled by the power of thought, could have become the ideal army — tireless, needing no resources, incapable of betrayal... But it was Nomarkh Sadaffee himself who became the traitor! According to the latest information, he managed to destroy or subjugate the entire guard of Zone 51. Contact with the military base was lost, and now nobody knows what is going on there. So if you see a pretty tropical islet in the Astral, where gloomy metal hangars peer out among the green jungle, know this — landing on that island may be the biggest mistake of your life... And quite possibly the last!

Bosses: Scar, Kiddo, Crash, Nomarkh Sadaffee.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

t: The Mausoleum of Sparks is an ancient structure built by Tep himself somewhere in the deep layers of the Astral. The mighty sorcerer used it as a place for mysterious experiments on the Sparks of ordinary inhabitants of Sarnaut. Thanks to the life energy contained in the Sparks, which was extracted by enormous devices, Tep could work true miracles…

t:
The land of Gipat, where your journey begins, resembles the temperate midlands in summer in its relief and vegetation. Beware of the apparent idyll and look around carefully; remember that Gipat's hostile and treacherous inhabitants are unpredictable! Trolls and goblins, bats, wolves, boars, hares and deer lie in wait for you. There are harpies too, in all their three-dimensional splendour. They are fabulously beautiful, but you must already know their foul temper well. More than once you will have to descend into natural caves, man-made mines and dungeons. Some of the dwellers of those worlds, who have never seen the sun or living people, will stay in your memory for a long time — if you manage to make it back to the surface, of course…

This island belongs to the group of orc islands. Its main population is orcs and goblins. The only village where people live is very small and constantly under threat of destruction. There is also a bandit camp whose members somehow manage to get along with the monsters. There is practically no metal here; people use bone and stone weapons and leather armour. Ruins of an unknown ancient civilization are found all over the island. It is small, and it belongs to none of the states because it is hard to reach and swarms with hostile monsters.

The Kanian Empire had plans to annex this land and had even built a fortress, but after the Cataclysm that split the world apart, the fortress and its garrison were left to fend for themselves. A handful of descendants of that garrison still live on Gipat, constantly fighting the goblins for the right to live.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t: Geographically, the allod of Yazes is divided into several regions, each with its own climate. The western part of the island is taken up by a forest (mostly oak groves) called the Ancient Forest. To its south-west lie the Lost Lakes, a mysterious land whose peoples do not obey the crown of Yazes. Formally the Ancient Forest is part of the kingdom, but its true masters are the druids. In addition, the elven city of Elliavan stands in the north-west of the allod. The south and south-east of Yazes are desert (most of it called the Hemer Desert), inhabited mainly by orc and goblin tribes united into several clans. Accordingly, the central and north-eastern parts of the allod are the territory of the kingdom of Yazes proper, populated mostly by humans.

t: Irdrich. An allod once kept in the Astral by a Great Mage (name unknown) who had locked himself in a time loop. It was later captured by Tep's cultists. It is notable for the newest of the pyramids built, the base of Tep's cultists and a huge complex for creating virtual reality. The climate was originally tropical; since Tep's capture it cannot be determined.

t: An island near the Pearl Ring, close to the Rainbow Atoll. On the island is a camp of anarchist Aviaks. The camp has a forge, a storehouse, a headquarters, a kitchen, a barracks and the anarchists' huts.

t: This place is well known — it has a bad name all across the Astral. The foremost pirate nest in the world! What bandits and cutthroats aren't there! Feint the Greedy himself moved there shortly before his death — they say he buried his treasure there too... Well, anyone can wag their tongue about pirate treasure. But the fresh rumours about that island are far worse. They say someone has finally found a way to deal with the buccaneers. A gentleman of fortune I know wanted to stop there and sell off his loot, but then he looks — smoke rising in a column, the fort in ruins, and above it what seem like bluish tentacles as thick as a mast swaying... In short, a decent person had no business there before, and now even less so!

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t: Dane. A neutral allod with a temperate climate. The allod is run by the oligarch Ivan Chelezny. It is home to one of the Demon Hunters' fortresses, called the "White" one, two large towns and an ancient elven palace. It is populated mostly by humans.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t:
It was quite different — there was no mountain with a cave in the middle.

An allod wrapped in a snowy blizzard. On arrival you come upon a Gibberling camp, and they tell you the legend of the island. Once, on this island, a legendary dragon hunter managed to kill one of the last dragons, but the monster's spirit is still alive, and the Gibberlings plan to get their hands on its treasures. Besides the dragon, there was also the ghost of a June hunter... by the way, that is the very Hunter who imprisoned Nordrak. So the storyline from the Frozen Frontier continued here.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t:
Not far from the landing site stands a village of neutral Waterfolk, whose chief sends you to find a tribesman captured by a group of aggressive kinsmen who worship some sea monster (Rybko).

"I dreamed of many things. I understood almost none of it. I dreamed of some terrible creature with a great beard, chained to the sky. I dreamed of monsters with tentacles on their faces... Oh, it's all so complicated" — this passage is interesting. It was long, long before Sarn appeared in the story, and back then hardly anyone understood it.

On the whole the story here is clear: one of the Sites of Power of the Holy Land (the Source of Cold Fire) broke away and gave power to the local Waterfolk, and they thought it was the Fish (later the scorpion Serket) that had given it to them, and began offering sacrifices to it.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t: This one was about the House de Doucer: what those who did not become vampires get up to. As I said before, the stories continued certain threads of the main storyline that had not been finished at the time... In some ways this island probably later became the basis for Enoch, which was indeed about vampires.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t: The island is being occupied by cultists who have recently arrived from a neighbouring allod. Quickly working out how the island is laid out, and meeting almost no resistance, they seize its only source of water. The orcs — the local population — have fallen back right up against the walls of their village, while the goblins, not a particularly courageous people, surrendered at once. You must free the allod from the usurping bandits and save the orc and goblin tribes. Here again it was a story about Tep. In general he was clearly also being lined up as a main enemy for the future.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t: A rather interesting island; there was a very long scripted quest chain here. Alas, it kept glitching and breaking... It was also called "The Lady", after the main boss. I hope the quests make it clear who says what... As you can see, there was a choice here — to kill Otrad or Verona. In general you can see how much everything relied on scripts and with what difficulty it worked in those days. Most people got stuck at the point where we reached the Gibberlings and walked into an ambush — the ambush simply never appeared.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t: Speaking of this island, it is a great pity it was never introduced. It continued the Gibberlings' storyline about the search for their Homeland, putting a full stop to that story, and it had an atmosphere all of its own. The quests were given by the Gibberling Yodo, the Great Master. The idea is that it really is a chunk of rock on which the Great Tree is hidden under a dome. That is why, so to speak, it was never found.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t: It is also known as the Isle of Suckers. It lay in the League's home sector, so many League players know it well: there were the sucker Forestfolk and their chief Barefoot, and of course the orc smuggler, from whom we carried off a heap of loot! Here too you can see that the writers had given some thought to why these islands exist in the astral at all. It is not clear, though, how this island existed before those crates were brought to it.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t: It lay somewhere very deep in the astral, so few people saw it. Though I believe a playthrough was lying about somewhere on YouTube. There is mention of a sphere with which an allod could be protected from the advance of the astral. And it is precisely such a Sphere that is used to protect this colony.

t: There was a bugged boss there, so everyone usually flew away from it. And I think it was also in the League's starting sector. After the rework the story there is roughly the same, although Tep was no longer mentioned.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t:
Thinking of joining the Historians, are you? Any Historian would give his right hand without a second thought to explore Koch-Itzmahl.

Just imagine — a fully preserved temple from the heyday of the June empire. Not those pitiful ruins scattered everywhere, but a complete temple complex.

I confess I only glimpsed it, and even so I nearly fell overboard in amazement! Bas-reliefs, frescoes, statues, carved columns... Ah, and how many secrets it hides, how many treasures... Only there's no way to get at them!

Lizards have overrun the whole island. When we tried to land, they pelted us with spears, burned a huge hole in the sail with a fireball, and kept promising to tear out our hearts and lay them on the altar of their ancestors. Their chief, Shisskh, raged most of all. Ooh, vicious creatures!

We had to turn round urgently and move on empty-handed.

Clearing the temple of the lizards' presence is a good deed and pleasing to the Light... and a profitable one besides!

Bosses: Caiman, Lion, Bloodberry, Shisskh the Seven-Fingered.

t:
The Allod of Copperlock

It is the home of the Kudiyar race. Once, in the ancient times of the Old Era, there lived a small tribe of Kudiyars. They led a secretive life and tried not to leave the forests, especially in daylight, for danger lurked all around. Their leader is Jeter, a young albino kudiyar, the successor to his father's rule.

The allod is divided into three parts:

The Centre is the most important structure in Copperlock. It houses various stations and workshops, the departure point of the cable car and all the government institutions. The only things the Centre lacks are dwellings and shops. All of those lie along the whole length of Copperlock's street.

The Working Allod

The neighbouring allods serve an economic purpose. Mining meteorite ore allowed the kudiyars to build airships capable of travelling from one allod to another. As already mentioned, two cable cars run downward from the Centre of Copperlock, each ending on a different outlying allod. One line runs through all the levels of the city and stops at every station. It leads to the Working Allod. On the Working Allod the kudiyars, naturally, work. There is a farm, sown fields, a port for building airships and mines for extracting ore. The kudiyars travel to this allod precisely to work.

The Allod of the Red Forest

The second cable car leads to the second allod, the Red Forest. It was on this allod that the kudiyars found themselves after the Cataclysm. It is covered with trees of extraordinary red foliage. Wild animals live in the forest.

Version 0.1 – The first version of the project.

Version 0.2 – Added the map of Irene Palace. Filled in the Ferris section and astral island 76 (thanks to Evpraksiya). Lots of small fixes and improvements. Initial layout of the raids. Updated the description of Grok. Added the islands from Evpraksiya's list.

Version 0.3 – Added more astral islands from the early (beta) versions of AO (thanks to Rpikt), added descriptions to most of the astral islands. Improved some descriptions (thanks to Evgeny Ptitsyn). Added descriptions to some story islands (from AA, for those that had them). Added the map of Goblinball Stadium. Updated Irene (current versions of the maps). The “Unsorted” section was updated. The Pearl Ring was filled in, the Interreality was added. Some old versions of island maps appeared. Lots of small fixes and improvements.

Version 0.4 – Added Freedom Isle (the anarchist aviaks of the Pearl Ring). Added the fan allod Copperlock. Fixes to Ferris and Ammer. Added descriptions of the islands near Umoir. Improved the list and the descriptions of the open-beta islands. Added boss lists for the Astral Islands and the Reflections. Added the island of Suslanger from AO times. Added the Mausoleum of Sparks and the Arena of Heroes. Added the never-released Free City (Tortuga).

Version 0.5 – Added the Astral Trading Post, the Astral Factory, the Astral Manufactory, The Thing (beta island), Liberation (beta island); updated the Zalesky Patrimony island (beta island) and the Refuge of the Outcasts. Minor changes and additions.
